readiness.title: Readiness before training
readiness.desc: Answer how things are right now. Bodyweight and sleep hours are optional.
readiness.guideTitle: How do I fill this in?
guide: Fill it in before warming up, ideally at your usual time.
Use the descriptions on each scale and compare your answers with your previous days, not other athletes.
Stress, fatigue and stiffness: higher means more trouble. Sleep and food: higher means better. Answer honestly, not how you think your coach wants you to.
The readiness score combines your answers; it is not a strength test or a diagnosis. For pain, injury or illness, note where, when and how it affects you. Talk to your coach and seek care if needed.
examples: Slept 5 hours, stressful work week, legs heavy after last session: sleep quality 3, work stress 8, fatigue 7.
Normal day, ate well, slightly stiff hips this morning: everything around 5, nutrition 7, stiffness 6.
Day off, slept 8 hours and feel fresh: fatigue 2, sleep quality 8, stress 2–3.
readiness.notesPh: E.g. left knee hurts in squats, ill at the weekend, new work hours

work: No work or school pressure. You can switch off.
A little to do, with plenty of time and control.
Some tasks or a deadline, but manageable.
Quite busy. You sometimes think about it outside work.
Moderate pressure. It takes effort to keep up.
High workload. Hard to stop thinking about work or school.
Clear stress. Hard to concentrate or unwind.
Very high pressure, such as multiple deadlines or overtime. Recovery is affected.
Almost overwhelming. Work or school drains you even during time off.
Overwhelming pressure. Very hard to relax and recover.
life: Life outside work and school feels calm. No particular worries.
Small everyday issues, but easy to put aside.
Some worries or errands, but manageable.
Some pressure from family, finances or practical matters.
Moderate everyday stress. You often think about things to sort out.
Daily life takes a lot of energy. Hard to rest properly.
Worries or conflicts clearly affect energy and concentration.
High stress outside work. Sleep or recovery is affected.
Almost overwhelming, with few calm moments.
Overwhelming life stress. You feel unable to keep up or cope with the situation.
fatigue: Very fresh. Your body feels rested.
Slightly tired, but everyday movement feels easy.
Noticeably tired from the day or previous training, with plenty of energy left.
Moderately tired. Your body feels a little heavy, but everyday tasks are fine.
Clearly tired. Stairs and everyday movements take more effort than usual.
Very tired. Your body feels sluggish and you need more breaks.
Extremely tired. Simple physical tasks feel demanding.
Almost exhausted. Very little physical energy left.
Exhausted. Even simple everyday movements feel very demanding.
sleepQ: Almost no continuous sleep. Not rested at all.
Very poor night with trouble falling asleep or many long awakenings.
Poor, broken sleep. Clearly tired on waking.
Below your usual quality. Several awakenings or restless sleep.
Okay night. Some interruptions, but some recovery.
Fairly good sleep. A few minor interruptions; fairly rested.
Good night. Mostly continuous sleep; fairly fresh on waking.
Very good sleep. Few interruptions; clearly rested.
Almost uninterrupted sleep. Woke fresh and recovered.
Excellent night for you. Slept peacefully and woke fully rested.
nutrition: Almost no food or fluids in the last day.
Missed most meals and drank very little.
Clearly too little food and fluids, such as only one small meal.
Missed a main meal or ate little for most of the day.
Had several meals and fluids, but amounts or regularity could be better.
Ate fairly regularly and drank reasonably well. One meal was small.
Regular meals with enough food and fluids for most of the day.
Ate well, including protein and carbohydrates, and drank regularly.
Food and fluids matched your training and activity very well.
Enough regular, varied food for your day. No missed meals or clear feelings of dehydration.
stiffness: No stiffness or muscle soreness. You move freely.
Slight stiffness at first, easing almost immediately.
Mild stiffness or soreness with little effect on movement.
Noticeable stiffness, such as in the first squat or when standing up.
Moderate stiffness or soreness. A little movement helps you loosen up.
Clear stiffness. Some movements feel restricted or take more time.
Very stiff or sore. Bending, stairs or arm movements are affected.
Extremely stiff. You clearly change movements to work around the restriction.
Severe stiffness or soreness. Everyday movements are difficult.
Extreme stiffness or soreness. Everyday movement is very restricted.
soreness: Sore enough that warm-up feels heavier.
Very sore, hard to move freely.

readiness.gradesNote: These descriptions are examples to help you choose, not medical thresholds. Pick the closest and use the scale consistently from day to day.
readiness.stiffnessNote: Rate stiffness and muscle soreness, not sharp pain. Describe pain and its location in the note.
readiness.sleepQNote: Rate how you slept and how rested you felt on waking. Enter sleep hours separately.
readiness.nutritionNote: Rate whether you had enough food and fluids for your day, not whether the food was “perfect”.
